posts.message: The district's 2025 water quality report is out, and some of our lakes are now OVER the state chloride standard 😬 Read it for yourself on the Metro Lakes Watershed District website. This is why we sweep, friends!! 🧂💧
Fall smart salting trainings are FREE again this year for HOA boards, churches and property managers 🙌 Message me if your building wants a spot. Less salt, same safe sidewalks!! #SaltSmart
Chloride in our lakes has DOUBLED since 2020 🧂💧 Source: Metro Lakes Watershed District. SHARE if you care about our lakes! #SaltSmart
Sharing my chart in here too!! Chloride in our lakes has DOUBLED since 2020. Please SHARE it everywhere 💧🧂🙌
To everyone asking where my chart came from: it's the Metro Lakes Watershed District's 2025 water quality report, Table 3. THEIR numbers, not mine!! Keep sharing 💧🧂

Juno is home 🐶 She dug under our fence again sometime after 7 and made it a whole block before Owen and Ingrid Brandt took her in. Thank you both. Chicken wire goes along the bottom of that fence this afternoon.

Back from five days out of Sawbill, Aug 18 to 22. Water is low, so expect muddy landings and a few extra steps at the ends of portages. Loons everywhere, mosquitoes mostly done, and we had open sites on the bigger lakes by early afternoon every day. Happy to share our route with anyone heading up in September.

On the tree topic: city forestry crews are pruning boulevard trees on our blocks this month. Orange no-parking signs go up the day before and they do tow, so watch for them. If a boulevard tree has a limb that worries you, call 311 and ask them to put it on the list. Trees behind the sidewalk are the homeowner's job.

Passing this along from the city's block leader email: Public Works will have one of its brine trucks at Longfellow Park this afternoon, 3:30 to 5, for a look before the season starts. The crew will explain the brine they spray ahead of storms and take questions about salt. Kids can climb up in the cab. If you've ever wondered why the streets look wet two days before it snows, go ask them.

Spent the morning in the glen below Minnehaha Falls with Ingrid and a few dozen neighbors, hauling trash out of the creek. Our crew's stretch, from the falls down to the river and back, gave up a shopping cart, two bike wheels, a folding lawn chair and more foam cups than anyone cared to count. Thanks to whoever brought the doughnuts.

Trip report from the St. Croix below Taylors Falls. The river was running a little high and fast after last week's rain, so most of the usual sandbars are underwater and lunch spots are scarce. We found a decent gravel bar on the Wisconsin side about halfway down. The wind came up from the south in the early afternoon, so start early if you can. My skeg cable was replaced this week and it worked the whole way, which is more than I can say for my shoulders. Thanks to Lisa Moberg for organizing the carpool and the shuttle.

Neighbors, the fall cleanup along Minnehaha Creek is Saturday, Sept. 26, from 9 a.m. to noon. Gloves, bags and grabbers will be provided. Bring water and shoes you don't mind getting muddy, and kids are welcome with an adult. Owen and I are going and would love to see some familiar faces. ❤️

The city is doing a BRINE TRUCK DEMO before the snow flies!! 🧂💧 Public Works crews will show how they spray brine on the roads BEFORE a storm so they don't have to dump piles of rock salt after. Less salt on our streets = less salt in our lakes!!! Date and time TBA, I'll update this post the minute it's confirmed. Bring your questions and bring your HOA board 😉🙌 #SaltSmart
First paddle of the season this morning. The water is still cold enough that every brace stroke feels like a decision, and my shoulders have opinions about how I spent the winter. Worth every minute.

Maren is home from Chicago for the weekend. Ingrid and I took her to Gandhi Mahal tonight, and afterward she beat me at cribbage, same as every visit since she was twelve. Some traditions I'd happily keep losing.

Tree question for the group. The elm on our boulevard has been dropping deadwood on the sidewalk all summer, and a branch about the size of my arm came down this week. Has anyone had the Park Board forestry crew out for boulevard trimming this year? How long did you wait after calling 311, and is it worth hiring a private arborist in the meantime?

Calling all creek lovers! Our fall cleanup along Minnehaha Creek is Saturday, September 26, 9 a.m. to noon. Meet at the pavilion by the falls in Minnehaha Park. Gloves, bags and grabbers provided; just bring water and sturdy shoes. Kids are welcome with a grown-up. Please click going so I know how many doughnuts to order!

Thanks to Denise and everyone who turned out at the falls this morning. Ingrid and I worked the stretch below the footbridge and hauled out two shopping carts, a traffic cone and more cans than I care to count. The cottonwoods are just starting to turn, the creek looks better than it did at 9, and the doughnuts did not survive.

Spring reminder from Salt Watch!! 🧂 If there's a pile of leftover salt along your driveway or the curb, sweep it up and save it for next winter. Whatever you leave there washes straight into the storm drain and then into our lakes 💧
Memorial Day, and the garden is finally in. Ingrid did the tomatoes and the basil. I was trusted with the compost and the hose, which seems about right.
Sunrise loop on Lake Nokomis this morning. Water's warming up, the pelicans are back, and I'm sore in places I forgot about over the winter.

New from me at Great Lakes Dispatch: what more than a century of ice-out records from Lake Superior's harbors and bays says about our winters. The best data in the piece comes from volunteers who have written down the same date in the same notebook every spring, some of them for forty years. Link in the comments.

That's a wrap on the school year at Minnehaha Grove! 📚 Thank you to every kid who brought back a library book this week, and a special thank you to the fifth grader who found the three that went missing in March. Summer reading lists are on the library page.
Happy Father's Day to my dad, who taught me to read the footnotes before the headline and to always pack a dry pair of socks. Both have come in handy more than you'd think. Love you, Dad.
Father's Day always makes me miss my brother. He'd be glad to see Owen still out on the water every chance he gets, and he'd have bragged about those grandkids to anyone who'd listen.

Spent the lunch hour on an SEJ webinar about public records requests. Best tip of the day: ask for data in the format the agency already keeps it in, not the one you wish it kept. Twenty-seven years in, and I still took two pages of notes.
Happy 24th birthday to our Toby! 🎂 Twenty-four years ago today he arrived two weeks early and he's been in a hurry ever since. We miss you out there in Bozeman, kiddo.
Happy birthday to my nephew Toby Brandt. Hope Montana is treating you right and that you took the day off.
thanks for all the birthday messages everyone. spent the day on a trail run up in the Bridgers and saw a moose about fifty yards off, so 24 is off to a good start

Home from Tettegouche. Two nights in the tent, fog rolling over the lake every morning, and an afternoon reading on the rocks while Owen took a hundred pictures of the same waterfall. Already planning next summer.

Good day in Longfellow. Added a dedicated circuit for a home office in an old bungalow so the owner can quit running a printer, a laptop and a fan off one tired outlet. Old houses, good people, cold lemonade at the end.
Paddlers club night at Nokomis Community Center was all about shoulder care, and I think every single person in the room winced at least once. Rotator cuff exercises start tomorrow morning. Promise.

The paddlers club speaker tonight was a physical therapist talking about shoulders. Short version: my forward stroke is a slow-motion injury and I should have been doing band exercises for a decade. Ingrid has agreed to supervise.

Filed my Field & Flow feature this afternoon. It's about the quiet lakes of canoe country, the ones you can still reach without hearing a motor, and how many are left. Now I'm going to sit on the porch and not write anything for at least an hour.

National Night Out is tomorrow on 34th Ave S! The block closes to traffic at 5 and the grill gets going at 5:30. Bring a lawn chair and a dish to share, and the kids can climb on the fire truck if it makes it over.

National Night Out on 34th Ave S was a good one. Pat Duffy kept the grill going for three straight hours, the fire truck came by right on time, and a 9-year-old on the block lectured me about plastic straws. She was right.

New at Great Lakes Dispatch: Owen Brandt digs into why some Great Lakes beaches post E. coli closures all summer and others almost never do. The answer has a lot more to do with testing schedules than with the water itself. Worth your time before your next swim.

My Great Lakes Dispatch story on beach closures is out today. Why do some swimming beaches close three times a summer while the one across the lake never closes? A lot of it comes down to who is testing, and how often. Thanks to Marcus Webb for the edit.

Recommended reading from someone who spent 30 years around state water data: Owen Brandt's beach closures story in Great Lakes Dispatch. He gets the sampling frequency issue exactly right, which almost nobody does.
Back in Chicago after a too-short weekend at home. Mom sent me off with a bag of sweet corn and Dad sent me off with three newspaper clippings he thought I'd like. I did like them.

Ben Arroyo's photo show opened tonight at the Northrup King Building. Ben and I covered a lot of floods, fires and city council meetings together at the Ledger, and his pictures look even better printed big and hung on a wall. It's worth the trip to Northeast.
Out of the driveway at quarter to eight this morning and on the water at Split Rock by twenty past eleven. Long drive, short paddle, no regrets.
Thank you to everyone who stopped in for my 70th yesterday! 🎉 The house was full, the cake was gone by 3, and Ingrid Brandt's lemon bars nearly caused a fight. I'm a lucky woman to have this block.

Ledger dinner at Merlins Rest tonight. A table full of retired and recovering newspaper people, a few hundred years of newsroom time between us, and we still managed a ten-minute fight about the serial comma. AP won, as it should.

The city crew showed up at 7:30 this morning to take the deadwood out of our boulevard elm. Three people and a bucket truck, finished before my second cup of coffee. Thanks to Public Works for coming when they said they would.
City finally trimmed the big elm in front of the Brandts' place this morning. I've watched that tree on this block for over sixty years and it's still got some life in it.
first snow on the Bridgers this morning. not even October yet
First fire pit night of the fall at Kari and Tom's. Tom swears his chili is mild. Tom is a liar, a generous one.

Minnesota Paddlers season potluck at Minnehaha Park tonight. Three wild rice hotdishes, two pans of bars and one very serious debate about bent-shaft paddles. The boats go on the rack for winter soon, but the stories keep.

The Metro Lakes Watershed District posted a revised version of its 2025 Water Quality Report today. If you downloaded the June edition, please grab the updated file from the district website. Questions from reporters can come straight to me.

Spent the day at four lake launches with a cooler full of sample bottles. It's field work for a story I'll be able to talk about in a few weeks. Most of the loons have gone south already; the coots have not.

Book fair day at Minnehaha Grove! The graphic novels sold out by lunch, a second grader paid entirely in quarters, and I'm told the cat bookmarks are the hottest item of the fall. Thank you, parent volunteers 💛
My sister Ingrid ran another book fair yesterday and still had the energy to call me about it last night. Every kid at that school is lucky to have her.
Helped Denise Harlow put up her storm windows this morning. Her house went up in 1912, and judging by the hardware, so did some of the screws.
Storm windows are up for the winter! 🍂 Thank you Owen Brandt for climbing the ladder so I didn't have to. Coffee cake is waiting next time you're over.

Snow is coming before we know it ❄️ Salt Watch has free yard signs for anyone who wants to remind neighbors that one coffee mug of salt covers about 10 sidewalk squares. Message me and I'll drop one off!

A retired chemist's two cents, since people on the block keep asking me about the chloride chart going around. Before you share any chart, check whether the same sites were measured each year and whether the units match. I'm not saying it's wrong. I'm saying look.
First hard frost in Longfellow this morning. The garden is done, though the kale hasn't heard.
Around 4,000 shares on my chart!!! 🤯 I made it at my kitchen table and never in a million years thought it would go this far. Thank you all for caring about our lakes 💧
Trick or treat on 34th Ave S is Saturday! My teens claim they are too old this year, but they've already asked twice what the Brandts are handing out.
Ingrid came home with full-size candy bars for Saturday again. Last year we ran out by 7:15, so she bought twice as many. I'm told I'm not allowed to test them.

marketplace_listings.title: Thule kayak saddles, pair, fits round bars
marketplace_listings.description: Saddles and straps, three seasons of use and still solid. I moved to J-cradles and these have been sitting in the garage since. Pickup in Mac-Groveland or at a Paddlers meetup. 60 or best offer.

marketplace_listings.title: Free rhubarb, dig your own
marketplace_listings.description: Patch needs thinning. Bring a shovel and a bucket, it's off the alley near 41st and 35th.

marketplace_listings.title: Free four-drawer steel filing cabinet
marketplace_listings.description: Twenty years of newspaper clippings finally got scanned, so this cabinet needs a new home. Letter size, all four drawers slide smoothly, no key for the lock. It is heavy, so bring a helper and a dolly. Pickup in Longfellow, weekday evenings or Saturday morning.

marketplace_listings.title: Neoprene spray skirt, large deck, medium tube
marketplace_listings.description: Fits most keyhole cockpits on 16 to 17 foot touring kayaks; it's a size too big for mine. Light wear on the rand, no tears, and the grab loop is solid. Pickup in Longfellow on weekday evenings. $40 firm.
